exampleAnswers.title: Expressing a Position Vector in Component Form

question.text: Find the position vector of $R( 2,4 )$ in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}.$
question.explanation:
Our vector is shown in the diagram below.

Remember that in general, if a point $R$ has coordinates $(r_x,r_y),$ then its position vector is given by

\[ \overrightarrow{OR} = r_x\mathbf{i}+r_y\,\mathbf{j}. \]

Here, the point $R$ has coordinates $(2,4),$ so its position vector is given by \[ \begin{align*} \overrightarrow{OR} &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2} \,\mathbf{i}+ \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}\,\mathbf{j}. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Expressing a Position Vector in Component Form

question.text: Find the position vector of $R( -4,5 )$ in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}.$
question.explanation:
Our vector is shown in the diagram below.

Remember that in general, if a point $R$ has coordinates $(r_x,r_y),$ then its position vector is given by

\[ \overrightarrow{OR} = r_x\mathbf{i}+r_y\,\mathbf{j}. \]

Here, the point $R$ has coordinates $(-4,5),$ so its position vector is given by \[ \begin{align*} \overrightarrow{OR} &= (-4) \cdot \mathbf{i} + 5 \cdot \mathbf{j} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-4} \,\mathbf{i}+ \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}\,\mathbf{j}. \end{align*} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Expressing a Position Vector in Angle Bracket Notation

question.text: The point $W$ is shown in the picture above. Find the coordinates of the corresponding position vector.
question.explanation:
For a point with coordinates $(a_x, a_y),$ the position vector is $\left< a_x, a_y \right>.$

The point $W$ has coordinates $(1.5,-2.5),$ so the position vector is \[ \overrightarrow{OW} = \langle 1.5,-2.5 \rangle. \]
